The End of Memories bundle features three incredible indie titles, including A Space for the Unbound. Don't miss it!

Hello, Space Divers!
We’re excited to announce our latest indie collaboration: the End of Memories bundle. If you're craving unforgettable stories, you're just in time for it. This bundle features three titles that will immerse you in heartwarming tales, emotional conflicts, and thrilling adventures, leaving you wanting more. Created by different indie studios, each game brings its own unique narrative and beautifully crafted art, offering distinct experiences you don't want to miss.

Grab the End of Memories Bundle here!
https://store.steampowered.com/bundle/45126/

The bundle also includes Last Time I Saw You, the debut title from Maboroshi Artworks. The story unfolds in a reimagined vision of late 1980s Japan, where the main character, Ayumi, embarks on a coming-of-age journey, his first step toward adulthood. Inspired by Japanese mythology, you’ll encounter a diverse cast of characters along the way—from ordinary friends to kleptomaniac kappas. Will you be able to face the curse haunting Ayumi’s hometown?

The other game featured in the bundle is Until Then, a title released this year. Follow Mark’s journey in a world recovering from catastrophe as he navigates the ups and downs of high school life—meeting friends, practicing piano, racing to meet homework deadlines, and scrolling through social media while commuting. Explore themes of love, loss, and friendship as you experience Mark's everyday life and witness his growth and desire to become a better person. Immerse yourself in a cinematic experience, inspired by the recent past of Philippine locations and culture.

Check out all the games included in the End of Memories Bundle!

In her deep loneliness, she met another person who shared her pain.

notes.title: Devlog: The Story Behind A Space for the Unbound
notes.content:
Hello, everyone!

I’m Dimas, the art director of A Space for the Unbound.

My team and I recently did an interview for Indie Obscura, we talked about behind the scenes of A Space for the Unbound there. You can check out the video here and give it a like!

https://youtu.be/ZvnTWJ5lrH8

The Inspiration

After the interview, I feel like I want to share the story behind A Space for the Unbound here, too. So here it goes!

A Space of the Unbound started off as an internal game jam in 2015. Back then, there’s no really a clear vision on what the gameplay would be, and then I just made a very experimental one and a concept trailer. After it garnered some attention we decided to continue this project. You can see the initial build of A Space for the Unbound - The Bridge we made back in 2015 here:

https://mojiken.itch.io/a-space

Back to the topic. As for the overall experience, initially, I just want to tell a story about a girl who has a deep secret while she is seemingly living her happy daily life. The inspiration comes from a lot of movies, manga, and anime. Some of them are based on a slice of life genre and there’s also magical realism genre, too. I was inspired by a lot of movies such as Inception (Christopher Nolan) and The Truman Show (Peter Weir), and then manga by Oshimi Shuuzo-sensei also a novel The Strange Library by Haruki Murakami-sensei. And I want to combine all those inspirations with Indonesian culture and setting.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36262819/785a6e308e12d2e3edf3e33bac8645f5a4216605.jpg

90s Indonesia

Why 90s Indonesia rural setting?
Actually, the 90s wasn’t really the initial plan. As someone who grew up watching anime and born in the 90s, I just really want to preserve all the good times I had back in the day.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36262819/e950fc801a3e5b40e411cf27defc7f0123107f64.jpg

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36262819/fad56a8b621e299342b434e071121c1275913958.jpg


When I was in high school, I was blown away by Makoto Shinkai-sensei’s work and I discovered that he uses a lot of real-life locations, and at that time I realized that a lot of anime also does that too. Back in the day I also discovered an activity named  anime pilgrimage. A group of people doing a tour to real-life locations and compare the location with the animation scenes counterpart, and it inspires me a lot. I mean, if we can visualize and transform our environment, our hometown in a new, different way, in this case, pixel art, maybe we can appreciate the place we live in more, and we can add some new value to it.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36262819/62e180f02e67cf1fcb190c2ba253da43085d8a3e.png


It’s a really fun process! After narrowing down all the ideas, we came up with the keyword “90s” because as I mentioned before, we want to give a tribute to the time when we grew up.

I think that’s all for now! I will come back again with more stories on A Space for the Unbound next time! Thank you to everyone who has played the prologue and wishlist the game! We will do our best to work on the game and enjoy the process.

Terima kasih!


Dimas and Mojiken team
